title: What Forms of Student Sensemaking Predict Mathematics Learning?: Student Perspectives on Opportunity, Comfort, and Utility
summary: Instructional practices that require student sensemaking of mathematics are considered critical to learning outcomes, yet strategies for measurement of this instruction at scale have yet to be established. This study aims at validating and exploring the predictive validity of three student survey measures: students' opportunity to engage with, comfort engaging with, and utility of engaging with instructional practices targeting sensemaking in mathematics.
